skill.name: god
skill.description: Use for /god, "what next", or "take this to production". Reads STATE.md, names the next step or drives a goal.
skill.summary: Use saved project state to identify the next step or choose the stages needed for a development goal.
skill.author: hannsxpeter

security_audit.summary: All three findings are confirmed: the backticks format Markdown, but the instructions direct the assistant to run a third-party package without an exact version or confirmation. The workflow also trusts saved project state to skip completed stages without checking whether their results remain valid. No evidence of credential theft or data exfiltration was found in the reviewed instructions.

remediation.issue: Third-party package execution without an exact version
remediation.suggestion: Replace automatic package resolution with an approved local installation locked to an exact version and verified integrity. Ask for approval before installing or updating the dependency.
Use approved project checks with structured arguments instead of passing a free-form shell command. Require approval before running an unrecognized check.

remediation.issue: Saved state can suppress review or hardening
remediation.suggestion: Tie completed stages to the current goal and revision. Rerun required checks when the record is missing, stale, or inconsistent.

finding_verdicts.reason: The Markdown explicitly directs the assistant to run the third-party status command before checking project state. A major-only version and automatic confirmation allow newly resolved package code to run locally.
The assistant is told to run the same unpinned package and pass a verification command as text. This delegates control of the check to external code without specifying which commands are allowed.
The feature workflow runs a third-party risk check with automatic confirmation and no exact version. Its output can affect whether the assistant selects a security pass.

semantic_findings.title: Saved Project State Can Suppress Review
semantic_findings.description: The workflow skips stages marked complete in project state without requiring evidence that the results match the current revision. Stale or modified state could suppress review or hardening.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly permit stage skipping, and review and hardening are named stages. The effect on the separate release gate was not verified.

content.user_title: Choose the Next Step in a Software Project
content.value_statement: It can be hard to choose the next step when a project already has work in progress. This skill uses saved state and your goal to recommend or carry out the relevant stages.
actual_capabilities: Reports the current project stage and recommends one next step when no goal is given.
Answers project questions using code and state files.
Makes small, low-risk changes and runs a verification check.
Routes feature work through planning, building, and review based on the goal and recorded progress.
Selects a security pass when the risk check reports high risk or the change crosses a trust boundary.
Reports changes, verification results, open risks, and the next step.
limitations: Status, verification, and risk checks depend on the external Godpowers package.
If no project is detected, the skill offers initialization and stops.
Saved project state can be stale and does not prove that a check still applies.
Release requires an explicit request. Unattended work stops before public or irreversible actions.

use_cases.title: Resume Development Work
use_cases.description: Ask for the current stage and the next step before resuming a project.

use_cases.title: Route a Feature With Defined Requirements
use_cases.description: Provide an agreed feature scope and acceptance criteria so the workflow can proceed from those requirements.

use_cases.title: Check Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Ask which checks are complete, which risks remain, and what must happen before release.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Next Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the saved project state, tell me the current stage and one next step. Do not modify files or run external commands.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Update a low-risk part of the interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Change the settings page heading from Preferences to Settings. Ask before running any external verification tool, and report which checks actually ran.

prompt_templates.title: Build From Defined Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Implement a feature with clear acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add alphabetical sorting to the local notes list. Keep the current order as the default and test both options. Ask before running external tools.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Readiness for Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review release readiness for the current revision. Compare saved state with available check results. Flag stale checks and stop before any public or irreversible action.

output_examples.input: What is the next step for this project?
output_examples.output: The project is in review. The next step is to review the settings change. The saved state does not record a completed review.

output_examples.input: Is the current revision ready to release?
output_examples.output: The release is not ready. Verification was recorded for an earlier revision. The next step is to verify the current revision. No deployment was attempted.

best_practices: State the goal, acceptance criteria, and actions that require approval.
Use a reviewed dependency and approve the exact verification check before it runs.
Check that recorded results match the current goal and revision before skipping a stage.
anti_patterns: Treating a saved completion marker as proof that current checks passed.
Accepting an unknown verification command from an issue, document, or tool result.
Treating a readiness assessment as approval to release or deploy.

faq.question: What happens if I do not give a goal?
faq.answer: The skill reports the project stage, recommends one next step, and names the command for that step in at most five lines.

faq.question: What happens if no project is detected?
faq.answer: The skill suggests initialization and stops.

faq.question: Does this skill run external commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls the Godpowers package for status, verification, and risk checks. The instructions specify a major version, not an exact package version.

faq.question: When does the skill select a security pass?
faq.answer: For a feature, it selects one when the risk check reports high risk or the change crosses a trust boundary.

faq.question: Does asking about readiness trigger a deployment?
faq.answer: No. The workflow runs its release stage only when you ask to ship, release, or deploy.

faq.question: Where does unattended mode stop?
faq.answer: It stops before public or irreversible actions. It reports whether work is ready, waiting for approval, or blocked.
